lesson_title: Four Kitchens: SA's Industrial Regions, SDIs and IDZs
hook_text: A third of SA's economy sits on a plateau with no port and no river. How?
clip_script: Gauteng is the strangest industrial giant on earth. It has no port — a factory in Kempton Park sends its exports six hundred kilometres downhill to Durban before they touch a ship. It has no big river — its water is pumped up from the Vaal Dam and even from the mountains of Lesotho. By the textbook rules, nothing this size should stand there. So why is a third of the economy up on that plateau? Because of what the gold left behind: the railways still meet there, the skills still live there, the richest market in Africa still shops there. The giant outlived the gold that made it.
visual_style: Satellite zoom to the highveld at night blazing with light, water animating uphill from Lesotho's mountains, rail lines converging like veins on Johannesburg.
mood: Awe with a puzzle at its heart.
pacing: Pose the impossibility, stack the missing pieces, resolve with the gold's legacy.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — four core regions, two case studies, and the SDI and IDZ plans to spread the map.
